Components.Title: Component Hub
Components.Description: This screen consolidates the UI components that are usable right now in ToolboxWeb, grouped by component family. The live area focuses on interactive mini demos, while the Catalog clarifies which items are live-ready, asset-only, or missing from the current Kendo bundle.
Components.WidgetUnavailable: Widget is not available in the current bundle.
Components.LegacyKendoNote: Keeps the existing Kendo demo page intact for widget-by-widget reference.
Components.LegacyTabulatorNote: Keeps the original Tabulator batch CRUD screen intact for full save-flow testing.
Components.TextInputIntro: This family covers short text input, multiline input, and suggestion-enabled controls. Use native Bootstrap inputs for lighter forms, or the Kendo widgets when you want a more unified widget system.
Components.SelectionIntro: This family focuses on checkbox, single selection, multi-selection, and vertical pick-list controls. These are the most common building blocks for filters, metadata, and admin forms.
Components.DateTimeNumericIntro: This family is for date, time, and numeric input that benefits from clearer formatting and culture-aware behavior. The current source can mix native inputs and Kendo pickers depending on form complexity.
Components.GridDataIntro: This section reflects the current source convention: editable grids use Tabulator, while lighter list-data scenarios use Kendo DataSource + ListView + Pager instead of the commercial Grid.
Components.FeedbackPopupIntro: This family groups status messaging, tabbed content, client-side validation, and popup behavior for both lightweight and more focused user interactions.
Components.NavigationLayoutIntro: This family is for small menus, collapsible help areas, and resizable pane layouts. These widgets are useful when building configuration screens or multi-region workspaces.
Components.CatalogIntro: The catalog separates what is live-demoed, what is confirmed inside the current bundle, and what only exists as source assets. That makes it easier to choose the right library later without rescanning the full bundle.
Components.Catalog.BundleOnlyTitle: Kendo bundle confirmed but not live-demoed

SqlProfiler.Intro: Start recording, use your application, then come back to see which stored procedures ran.
SqlProfiler.Capture.HowTo: Press Start recording, switch to your application or website and use the feature you want to inspect, then come back and press Stop. Whatever reached the database in that window appears in the table below.
SqlProfiler.Recent.HowTo: This mode looks back without recording first. In exchange, SQL Server only keeps aggregate statistics, so it cannot say who called, from which machine, or with which parameters.

SeedPrompt.FeatureRequest.Name: Feature request
SeedPrompt.FeatureRequest.Description: Describe a new feature with scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria.
SeedPrompt.FeatureRequest.InputVariables:
feature description
user goal
in/out scope
constraints
acceptance criteria
SeedPrompt.FeatureRequest.OutputFormat:
1. Solution summary
2. Entity/service/controller/view impact
3. Migration impact
4. Tests or build commands to run
SeedPrompt.FeatureRequest.Content: Please read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md first. I need a new feature: [description]. User goal: [goal]. Scope: [in/out]. Constraints: keep controllers thin, put logic in Services, filter data by UserId, and preserve Content/ as the web root. Acceptance criteria: [list]. Propose the entity, service methods, controller actions, ViewModels, views, migration impact, and tests to run.
SeedPrompt.BugReport.Name: Bug report
SeedPrompt.BugReport.Description: Capture the bug, repro steps, impact, and expected behavior.
SeedPrompt.BugReport.OutputFormat:
1. Root cause
2. Proposed fix
3. User isolation/validation/migration impact
4. Tests to add or rerun
SeedPrompt.BugReport.Content: Please read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md first. The bug happens in module: [module]. Repro steps: [steps]. Current result: [actual]. Expected result: [expected]. Data or user context: [context]. Find the root cause, fix it in the correct layer, avoid unrelated refactors, and call out any impact on user isolation, validation, migrations, and tests.
SeedPrompt.MaintenanceHandoff.Name: Maintenance handoff
SeedPrompt.MaintenanceHandoff.Descriptio: Hand over module context to the next maintainer.
SeedPrompt.MaintenanceHandoff.OutputForm:

Service
Entity
ViewModels/Views
Data flow
Editing risks
Verification checklist
SeedPrompt.MaintenanceHandoff.Content: Summarize module [module name]: goal, controller, service, entity, related views, data flow, editing risks, and a post-change test checklist.
SeedPrompt.CodeReview.Name: Code review
SeedPrompt.CodeReview.Description: Review changes with a focus on bugs, risks, and test coverage.
SeedPrompt.CodeReview.InputVariables: branch, diff, or files to review
SeedPrompt.CodeReview.OutputFormat:
File/line findings first
Then remaining risks or test gaps
SeedPrompt.CodeReview.Content: Review this change in priority order: bugs, security, user isolation, validation, migrations, and test gaps. Respond with file/line findings first. If nothing is wrong, call out the remaining risks.
SeedPrompt.UiChange.Name: UI change
SeedPrompt.UiChange.Description: Describe a UI update while preserving the compact ToolboxWeb feel.
SeedPrompt.UiChange.InputVariables:
screen
goal
areas
grid alignment rules if a table is present
SeedPrompt.UiChange.OutputFormat:
1. Main UI changes
2. Razor/CSS/JS files to update
3. Responsive, localStorage, and grid alignment impact
4. Verification steps
SeedPrompt.UiChange.Content: I want to change the UI of screen: [screen]. Goal: [goal]. Areas to change: [areas]. If the screen contains a grid, use this convention: center the header labels, left-align text columns, right-align decimal or money columns, and center the remaining body columns. Keep the compact dashboard style, do not add a marketing landing page, preserve Content/ as the web root, keep preferences in localStorage, and account for desktop/mobile responsiveness. Propose the view, CSS, JS, and verification changes.
SeedPrompt.DatabaseChange.Name: Database change
SeedPrompt.DatabaseChange.Description: Describe a schema change, data risk, and how to verify the migration.
SeedPrompt.DatabaseChange.OutputFormat:
1. Model/DbContext changes
2. Required migration
3. Data compatibility risks
4. Build/migration/test verification commands
SeedPrompt.DatabaseChange.Content: I need to change SQLite schema because: [reason]. Related entities: [entities]. Existing data to preserve: [requirements]. Explain the entity, DbContext, and migration changes, the data compatibility risk, any user isolation impact, and the commands or tests needed to verify the change.
